newsitem.title: USA: Oglethorpe cleared to to buy LG&E power.
newsitem.headline: Oglethorpe cleared to to buy LG&E power.

text.p: Oglethorpe Power Corp said Friday it received approval from the Rural Utilities Service to buy electricity from LG&E Power Marketing under a 15-year agreement negotiated last November.
The approval clears the way for implementation of one of the largest long-term power marketing agreements ever signed in the United States, the company said.
The LG&E Energy Corp subsidiary will supply about half of Oglethorpe Power's system-wide power needs, and can market excess power from Oglethorpe Power's generating resources, the cooperative said.
Approval was necessary before the agreement could be implemented as a long-term arrangement.
LG&E has been supplying energy to Oglethorpe Power under a short-term arrangement since Jananuary 1.
Oglethorpe spokesman Greg Jones said the short term arrangement replaced short term power purchases the company had been making from Duke Power Co and Louis Dreyfus.

Oglethorpe Power said it is in the process of unbundling its services into three separate operating companies in preparation for a more competitive utility environment. This restructuring is scheduled to be completed during the first quarter of 1997.
In addition, the corporation said, it is pursuing a second power marketing deal to provide the other half of its power needs.
Oglethorpe Power provides wholesale electricity to 39 of Georgia's 42 customer-owned Electric Membership Corporations.
